title: Application Management
summary: Explains application catalog governance, create and rename patterns, and controlled retirement workflow.
coverage: Meaning of application owner vs maintainer
Impact of app rename/delete on assigned records

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Application definitions are shared grouping primitives across records and security workflows. Name and ownership hygiene at the application level prevents large-scale reporting and assignment drift.

sections.title: Application purpose
paragraphs: Application management establishes service boundaries used for grouping records and interpreting risk posture. A clean application catalog makes cross-record review, ownership governance, and workload planning significantly more reliable.
Applications are not cosmetic labels. They are organizational anchors used by both operational and security workflows.

sections.title: Manage Apps workflow
paragraphs: The Manage Apps dialog supports create, rename, and delete operations. Each operation should be treated as a controlled catalog change because it affects all records linked to the target application.
Rename operations are intended for canonicalization and service naming alignment. Create operations should follow a naming standard that reflects stable service identity.

rows: Introduce a new stable service grouping.
New application becomes selectable in record edit forms.
Correct naming drift or align with canonical service name.
Linked records adopt updated application display name.
Retire obsolete grouping that should no longer be used.
Linked records become unassigned and require reclassification.

sections.title: Owner and maintainer governance at app scope
paragraphs: Application-level governance requires consistency between record ownership values and service grouping intent. If an application contains many records with conflicting owner semantics, incident routing and remediation coordination become noisy.
Use app-level review sessions to harmonize owner and maintainer patterns across records in the same group.

sections.title: Rename and delete risk controls
paragraphs: Renaming or deleting applications can have broad downstream impact. Rename is generally safe when it preserves service identity. Delete should be reserved for verified retirement or accidental duplicate catalogs.
Before delete, confirm the list of linked records and define a reassignment plan so unassigned records do not accumulate.
orderedList: Identify the set of records currently linked to the application.
Confirm whether the app should be renamed or replaced.
If deleting, prepare target application mappings first.
Execute change and immediately reassign any ungrouped records.

sections.title: Naming standard recommendations
paragraphs: Use short, stable, service-oriented names. Avoid temporary project labels, personal names, or environment-only variants as top-level application names.
A practical pattern is `Service Name` for the application and environment-specific context in record metadata, not in application identity.
list: Use one app entity per stable service boundary.
Review duplicate names quarterly and merge where appropriate.
